en: Itivuttaka 107 The Chapter on Fours (Catukkanipāta) The Subchapter on the Brahmin’s Dharma-Sacrifice (Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga)
The Bahukāra Sutta.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
"Monks, the brahmin householders are of great service to you, for they provide you with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick."
You too, monks, are of great benefit to the brahmins and householders, in that you teach them the Dhamma— good in the beginning,
good in the middle, and good in the end— with the right meaning and phrasing; you proclaim the holy life in its entirety, perfectly complete and pure.
"Thus, monks, this holy life is lived in mutual dependence for the purpose of crossing over the flood and for the complete making an end of suffering.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“Both householders and the homeless, each depending on the other,
accomplish the true Dhamma.”
The unsurpassed security from bondage.
Among householders, robes,
requisites, and lodgings;
The homeless ones accept [this] for the dispelling of dangers,
having relied upon the Sugata.
Householders seeking a home,
having faith in the Arahants who meditate with noble wisdom.
Having practiced the Dhamma here,
the path that leads to a happy destination,
they rejoice in the world of the gods.
“Those who desire sensual pleasures rejoice.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The eighth [sutta].
